item.title: [general] How AI Assistants are Moving the Security Goalposts
item.description: AI-based assistants or "agents" -- autonomous programs that have access to the user's computer, files, online services and can automate virtually any task -- are growing in popularity with developers and IT workers. But as so many eyebrow-raising headlines over the past few weeks have shown, these powerful and assertive new tools are rapidly shifting the security priorities for organizations, while blurring the lines between data and code, trusted co-worker and insider threat, ninja hacker and novice code jockey.

item.title: [threat-intel] Who is the Kimwolf Botmaster “Dort”?
item.description: In early January 2026, KrebsOnSecurity revealed how a security researcher disclosed a vulnerability that was used to assemble Kimwolf, the world's largest and most disruptive botnet. Since then, the person in control of Kimwolf -- who goes by the handle "Dort" -- has coordinated a barrage of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS), doxing and email flooding attacks against the researcher and this author, and more recently caused a SWAT team to be sent to the researcher's home. This post examines what is knowable about Dort based on public information.

item.title: [general] ‘Starkiller’ Phishing Service Proxies Real Login Pages, MFA
item.description: Most phishing websites are little more than static copies of login pages for popular online destinations, and they are often quickly taken down by anti-abuse activists and security firms. But a stealthy new phishing-as-a-service offering lets customers sidestep both of these pitfalls: It uses cleverly disguised links to load the target brand's real website, and then acts as a relay between the target and the legitimate site -- forwarding the victim's username, password and multi-factor authentication (MFA) code to the legitimate site and returning its responses.

item.title: [malware] Kimwolf Botnet Swamps Anonymity Network I2P

I2P users started reporting disruptions in the network around the same time the Kimwolf botmasters began relying on it to evade takedown attempts against the botnet's control servers.

item.description: <p>In this Help Net Security interview, Christa Dodoo, Global Chair at IFMA, discusses how facility managers are managing supply chain risk in critical building systems. item.title: [general] Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel 8.2 ships with confidential computing support, XFS live repair
item.description: <p>Many enterprise Linux deployments rely on hardware-level memory isolation to protect sensitive workloads from co-tenants and compromised hypervisors. Oracle&#8217;s Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel 8.2 (UEK 8.2) extends that capability on Oracle Linux with support for Intel Trust Domain Extensions, along with a set of file system and memory management changes intended to reduce downtime and improve diagnostic visibility. UEK 8.2 is based on the mainline long-term stable Linux 6.12 kernel and carries the release number 6.12.0-200. &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/26/oracle-unbreakable-enterprise-kernel-8-2/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/26/oracle-unbreakable-enterprise-kernel-8-2/">Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel 8.2 ships with confidential computing support, XFS live repair</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [ransomware] Botnet operator behind $14 million in ransomware extortion payments gets 24 months behind bars
item.description: <p>A Russian national has been sentenced to 24 months in prison after admitting he managed a botnet used to launch ransomware attacks against dozens of U.S. companies. The judge also imposed a $100,000 fine and ordered him to forfeit $1.6 million linked to the scheme. item.title: [general] Vorlon adds forensics and response to secure AI agents
item.description: <p>Vorlon has unveiled AI Agent Flight Recorder and AI Agent Action Center, adding forensics and coordinated response to secure enterprise agentic ecosystems and close a key security gap. The agentic ecosystem contains SaaS applications, AI agents, API integrations, non-human identities, and the sensitive data flows connecting them. item.title: [general] As the US Midterms Approach, AI Is Going to Emerge as a Key Issue Concerning Voters
item.description: <p>In December, the Trump administration signed an executive order that <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/11/technology/ai-trump-executive-order.html">neutered</a> states&#8217; ability to regulate AI by ordering his administration to both sue and withhold funds from states that try to do so. This action pointedly supported <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/08/us/politics/trump-executive-order-ai-laws.html">industry lobbyists</a> keen to avoid any constraints and consequences on their deployment of AI, while undermining the efforts of consumers, advocates, and industry associations concerned about AI&#8217;s harms who have spent years pushing for state regulation.</p> <p>Trump&#8217;s actions have clarified the ideological alignments around AI within America&#8217;s electoral factions. They set down lines on a new playing field for the midterm elections, prompting members of his party, the opposition, and all of us to consider where we stand in the debate over how and where to let AI transform our lives...</p>
